_note: Maps a delivered capability to what it is worth in business language. The exec pack states the benefit and the reason, never the capability tag.

identity.pdp.central.benefit: One place to change who can do what
identity.pdp.central.why: A policy change lands everywhere at once instead of being reimplemented per application, which removes the drift that currently makes access questions expensive to answer.

identity.workload.federated.why: The credential class behind a large share of breaches stops existing, and the operational burden of rotating and reissuing secrets goes with it.

identity.privileged.jit.benefit: Standing privilege replaced by time-boxed access
identity.privileged.jit.why: The permanent administrative accounts that make lateral movement worthwhile are removed, and every elevation carries an approver and a recording.

identity.mtls.identity.benefit: Every connection proves who is on both ends
identity.mtls.identity.why: Trust stops being a property of the network, so reaching a system is no longer the same thing as being allowed to use it.

identity.subject-schema.benefit: Every security event names a real actor
identity.subject-schema.why: Investigations start with attribution instead of reconstructing it, which is the difference between hours and days on an incident.

identity.federation.external.benefit: Partner and customer access is governed centrally
identity.federation.external.why: External trust is inventoried and revocable rather than accumulated through point arrangements nobody owns.

identity.secrets.managed.benefit: Secrets have a lifecycle rather than a location
identity.secrets.managed.why: Issuance, rotation and revocation become routine operations instead of change requests, and expiry stops causing outages.

network.private.only.benefit: No public data path to attack
network.private.only.why: The external attack surface reduces to a deliberately chosen list rather than whatever happens to be reachable.

network.egress.inspected.benefit: Outbound traffic can be read, not just counted
network.egress.inspected.why: Data leaving the estate becomes something that can be controlled and detected rather than inferred from volume.

network.egress.fqdn-allowlist.benefit: Outbound goes only where it is meant to
network.egress.fqdn-allowlist.why: Named-destination control is specific in a way that IP ranges are not, so a shared cloud endpoint no longer implies permission for every tenant behind it.

network.segmentation.micro.benefit: A compromise stops at one service
network.segmentation.micro.why: Blast radius becomes a design property instead of an outcome, which is what materially reduces the cost of an incident.

network.dns.deterministic.benefit: Names resolve the same way on purpose
network.dns.deterministic.why: Environment-specific resolution becomes a decision on record rather than inherited behaviour nobody can explain during an incident.

network.ingress.waf.benefit: The public surface is actively defended
network.ingress.waf.why: Common attack classes are absorbed at the edge rather than reaching application code.

network.residency.pinned.benefit: Traffic stays where it is supposed to
network.residency.pinned.why: The routing and failover paths that most often breach a residency commitment are traced and constrained.

network.flowlogs.why: Detection and investigation have a source of truth about what actually connected to what.

network.reach.control-plane.benefit: Security services are reachable everywhere they are needed
network.reach.control-plane.why: Identity, policy and key services work the same way in every environment instead of failing in the one that was never tested.

data.key.customer-managed.benefit: The organisation controls its own encryption keys
data.key.customer-managed.why: Key custody is a position that can be evidenced to a regulator or a customer, rather than delegated to a provider by default.

data.key.hyok.benefit: Keys held outside the platform that processes the data
data.key.hyok.why: Compromise of the processing platform does not by itself yield readable data.

data.classification.per-flow.benefit: Controls follow the data, not the system label
data.classification.per-flow.why: Protection is applied where sensitive elements actually travel, closing the gaps a system-level label cannot see.

data.tokenised.benefit: Most of the estate never holds the sensitive value
data.tokenised.why: Assessment scope, breach impact and the cost of every downstream control fall together, because there is less to protect.

data.dlp.egress.benefit: Data leaving is controlled, not just observed
data.dlp.egress.why: Exfiltration becomes something the estate can stop rather than something it reports afterwards.

data.residency.in-region.why: Residency commitments to regulators and customers are backed by traced paths rather than by intent.

data.nonprod.synthetic.why: The single largest and least controlled data exposure in most estates is removed rather than mitigated.

data.nonprod.masked.benefit: Non-production data carries a stated guarantee
data.nonprod.masked.why: Test environments stop being an unmanaged copy of the customer base.

data.retention.policy.benefit: Data is disposed of when it should be
data.retention.policy.why: Retention becomes a control rather than an accumulation, which reduces both breach impact and storage cost.

data.access.audited.why: Questions about who saw what are answerable from evidence rather than from inference.

integration.edge.authz.benefit: Every boundary crossing is authorised on its merits
integration.edge.authz.why: Reaching a service stops implying permission to use it, which is what contains a compromise to its entry point.

integration.gateway.managed.benefit: One consistent policy layer across interfaces
integration.gateway.managed.why: Security behaviour is applied uniformly instead of reimplemented per integration with per-integration mistakes.

integration.contract.governed.why: Versioned contracts remove a recurring class of production incident and let teams release independently.

integration.async.idempotent.why: Retries and replays stop producing duplicated business effect, which is the failure mode that reaches customers.

integration.per-edge-logging.benefit: Every interface is visible to detection
integration.per-edge-logging.why: Integrations stop being the blind spot between two well-monitored systems.

integration.thirdparty.registered.benefit: Third-party dependency is known and governed
integration.thirdparty.registered.why: Materiality, concentration and exit are assessed before they are tested by an incident.

secops.log.type1.benefit: Threat detection can see this system
secops.log.type1.why: The central monitoring function has the sources its detections need, so an attack on this scope is something the organisation can find rather than something it learns about later.

secops.log.type2.why: The records a regulator, an auditor or an investigation will ask for are held on the enterprise compliance platform for the period the obligation requires, rather than expiring on a schedule nobody assessed.

secops.detection.identity.why: The most common route to material impact - misuse of legitimate credentials - is actively hunted rather than assumed absent.

secops.detection.egress.why: Exfiltration is detected in progress rather than reconstructed afterwards.

secops.nonprod.monitored.benefit: Non-production is no longer a blind spot
secops.nonprod.monitored.why: The environment with the weakest controls and often production-derived data is finally in scope for detection.

secops.soar.why: Containment starts at machine speed for the actions where that is safe, compressing the window an attacker has.

secops.ir.runbook.benefit: Incidents are handled to a known plan
secops.ir.runbook.why: Response quality stops depending on who is on call.

platform.provenance.signed.benefit: What runs can be traced to what was written
platform.provenance.signed.why: Supply-chain assurance becomes evidence the pipeline produces rather than a claim made in a document.

platform.admission.control.why: The gap between a governed build process and what is actually executing is closed.

platform.iac.governed.benefit: Infrastructure change is reviewable and reversible
platform.iac.governed.why: Configuration becomes a reviewed artefact instead of an accumulation of manual actions nobody can reconstruct.

platform.parity.pipeline.benefit: Testing in one environment predicts another
platform.parity.pipeline.why: The value of pre-production testing is restored, because the environments are actually comparable.

platform.runtime.protection.benefit: Workload behaviour is constrained at run time
platform.runtime.protection.why: Exploitation of an unknown vulnerability still has to get past a behavioural boundary.

platform.workload.identity.benefit: The platform can vouch for what is running
platform.workload.identity.why: Identity and network policy gain a trustworthy foundation instead of inferring identity from placement.

resilience.multi-az.benefit: Loss of a data centre is survivable
resilience.multi-az.why: The most common infrastructure failure stops being a customer-visible outage.

resilience.multi-region.benefit: Loss of a region is survivable
resilience.multi-region.why: The service can meet an impact tolerance that a single-region position cannot.

resilience.failover.tested.why: A measured failover time is what satisfies a supervisor; a designed one does not.

resilience.backup.tested.why: The recovery path is proven before it is needed rather than during an incident.

resilience.capacity.headroom.why: Growth and business peaks stop being incidents.

grc.control.mapping.benefit: Obligations are mapped to controls with named evidence
grc.control.mapping.why: Assurance questions have answers ready rather than triggering a discovery exercise.

grc.evidence.automated.why: Assurance cost falls and the evidence shows the control operating over time, not just being configured.

grc.exception.register.benefit: Accepted risk is visible and expires
grc.exception.register.why: Temporary compromises stop becoming permanent by silence.

grc.thirdparty.dora.benefit: Third-party obligations are met with exit plans
grc.thirdparty.dora.why: Concentration and dependency are managed before a supplier event forces the question.

grc.modelrisk.tiered.why: Scoring can be decomposed and challenged, which is what keeps decisions taken on it valid.

env.parity.asserted.benefit: Environment differences are decisions, not drift
env.parity.asserted.why: What passes in pre-production is meaningful evidence about production behaviour.

env.promotion.gated.why: Gates test stated properties instead of collecting signatures.

env.data.policy.benefit: Each environment holds only what it should
env.data.policy.why: The data exposure in lower environments is bounded by a control rather than by convention.

env.rtl.representative.benefit: Pre-production catches what production would hit
env.rtl.representative.why: Defects and failure modes surface before customers meet them.

secops.log.type3.benefit: The team can diagnose its own service
secops.log.type3.why: Operational telemetry is chosen deliberately against what running the service actually needs, instead of being an accident of what the security functions happened to require.

secops.ingestion.compatible.benefit: A future logging requirement is a connection, not a project
secops.ingestion.compatible.why: Security log requirements change as the threat landscape does. Building to the approved format, transport and authentication now means responding to that change costs days rather than a delivery cycle.

secops.requirements.registered.benefit: Both security functions know this system exists
secops.requirements.registered.why: Neither function can request a source it does not know is there. A current register entry is what turns their engagement model from reactive into informed.
